description.value: The study examined whether anodal tDCS over the left inferior frontal gyrus, combined with speech-language therapy, altered resting-state functional connectivity and whether connectivity changes were associated with improvements in written naming in people with primary progressive aphasia.

design.value: Participants came from a larger double-blinded, within-subject crossover clinical trial, but the present analysis used only the first stimulation phase in a between-subject design, comparing participants initially assigned to tDCS with those initially assigned to sham. Each condition consisted of 15 daily therapy sessions, and MRI and behavioral data were collected before and immediately after treatment.

description.value: Twenty-four participants with primary progressive aphasia took part in this study. All had a history of at least two years of progressive language deficits with no other etiology, atrophy predominantly in the left hemisphere, and no primary memory deficits. Participants were all right-handed and native speakers of English.

inclusion_criteria.value: A history of at least two years of progressive language deficits
No other etiology (e.g., stroke, tumors, etc.)
Atrophy predominantly in the left hemisphere
Right-handed and native speakers of English

clinical_characteristics.value: The groups were closely matched with regard to disease severity and the language component of severity based on the revised FTD-CDR. The two groups were also matched at baseline in language and cognitive task scores. There were 8 participants with lvPPA, 8 with nfvPPA, and 8 with svPPA.

description.value: Participants initially assigned to the tDCS condition, receiving anodal tDCS over the left inferior frontal gyrus and speech-language therapy.

clinical_characteristics.value: There were 5 participants with lvPPA, 3 with nfvPPA, and 4 with svPPA. Mean years post onset was 5.5 (3.5), mean language severity was 1.9 (0.9), mean total severity was 7.0 (4.5), and mean total treatment sessions was 13.3 (1.9).

description.value: Participants initially assigned to the sham condition, receiving a sham procedure paired with speech-language therapy.

clinical_characteristics.value: There were 3 participants with lvPPA, 5 with nfvPPA, and 4 with svPPA. Mean years post onset was 4.3 (2.4), mean language severity was 1.8 (0.7), mean total severity was 8.1 (5.4), and mean total treatment sessions was 13.5 (2.0).

task_description.value: The tDCS phase consisted of anodal tDCS over the left inferior frontal gyrus and speech-language therapy, while the sham phase consisted of a sham procedure paired with speech-language therapy. Each condition consisted of 15 sessions of daily therapy.

design_type.value: double-blinded, within-subject crossover design in the larger study; between-subject design for the first phase analyzed here

task_performance_measures.value: letter accuracy, i.e., percentage of letters corresponding to sounds making up words

task_description.value: Patients were shown a picture, asked to orally name the object, and then write it down. If they could not name the object, they were asked to provide three properties of the pictured item; if they still could not name it, the correct word was provided. Errors received corrective feedback and repeated opportunities to produce the name. Incorrect spelling was treated with a spell-study-spell procedure, rehearsing letters one by one and reinforcing learning by copying.

instructions.value: The patient was shown a picture on the computer, asked to orally name the object, and then write it down.

stimuli.value: Pictures of 10–30 words selected according to the level of language severity

task_performance_measures.value: percentage of correct letters in trained words

task_description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were acquired before, after, and two months post-intervention. Time-courses from 19 cortical and deep gray matter ROIs were extracted and correlations among them were calculated.

instrument.value: 3 T Philips Achieva MRI scanner equipped with a 32-channel head coil

description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were acquired using a 2D EPI sequence with SENSE partial-parallel imaging acceleration. The acquisition used SPIR for fat suppression and a 3 mm slice thickness.

instrument.value: 3 T Philips Achieva MRI scanner equipped with a 32-channel head coil

description.value: Structural scans were acquired axially using a T1-weighted MPRAGE sequence with 3D inversion recovery and magnetization-prepared rapid gradient. The scan was isotropic and had a 224 × 224 mm2 field of view.

The MPRAGE scan was processed in MRICloud using an atlas-based analysis approach. Each participant's high-resolution MPRAGE was segmented into 283 structures using multi-atlas fusion label algorithm and large deformation diffeomorphic metric mapping. All analyses were performed in native space, and ROI volumes were normalized by total intracerebral volume.

steps.value: Parcel the MPRAGE scan into 283 structures
Segment each participant's high-resolution MPRAGE using a multi-atlas fusion label algorithm
Apply large deformation diffeomorphic metric mapping
Normalize each ROI volume by total intracerebral volume

description.value: Resting-state fMRI was processed in MRICloud using routines imported from the SPM connectivity toolbox for coregistration, motion correction, and slice timing correction; physiological nuisance correction using CompCor; and motion and intensity TR outlier rejection using ART. After outlier exclusion, movement and physiological nuisance matrices were used in deconvolution regression for the remaining TRs. Structural parcels were coregistered to resting-state dynamics, and ROI time courses were extracted for correlation analysis.

steps.value: Detect motion and intensity TR outliers using ART, with parameters of 2 standard deviations for motion and 4 standard deviations for intensity
Use the movement matrix combined with the physiological nuisance matrix in deconvolution regression for the remaining TRs
Bring structural parcels into resting-state dynamics by coregistration
Extract time courses from 19 cortical and deep gray matter ROIs
Calculate Pearson correlations and Fisher z-transformed scores among ROIs

model_settings.value: Tests compared the difference between tDCS and sham groups in absolute change in percentage correct from before and after treatment.

model_type.value: semi-parametric method assembled with automated covariate selection

model_settings.value: For each pair of ROIs, the model used the z-transformed baseline correlation, age, sex, years post-onset, PPA variant, language severity, total severity of dementia using the FTD-CDR score, and left IFG volume before intervention as covariates. Forward model selection using Akaike information criterion was conducted separately for the tDCS and sham groups before combining them to estimate the average treatment effect. The standard sandwich estimator was used with adjustment for the small sample size, followed by Wald hypothesis testing and Holm family-wise error correction.

For each ROI pair with an unadjusted P-value less than .05 in the treatment-effect analysis, the before-and-after behavioral difference was regressed against the before-and-after functional-connectivity correlation difference, with an intercept.
Tests assessed within-group changes in percentage of correct letters after treatment.
